cards.prose: Luke tells what the dust is for. Matthew has the town that will not *receive you, nor hear your words*, and Luke's *for a testimony against them* says the shaking is a witness left standing at the door. The twelve are not sent after the town to argue it round; the word has been spoken, and they go out of the city.
cards.member_sentence: Matthew names the refusal as not receiving the twelve and not hearing their words, and has them shake off the dust as they leave.

cards.prose: Luke has the apostles just back and telling him *all that they had done*, and he takes them aside to a desert place by Bethsaida. Matthew says what sent him there, the news of John's death, and that the people *followed him on foot out of the cities*. So the lonely place is already filling with a crowd, and the twelve he has just taken aside will soon be the ones asked to feed it.
cards.member_phrase: and when the people had heard thereof, they followed him on foot out of the cities
cards.member_sentence: Matthew says why he withdrew, having heard of John, and that the crowds came after him on foot out of the cities.

cards.prose: Luke has him praying alone with the disciples near, and he asks *Whom say the people that I am?* with no place named. Matthew puts the same question at Caesarea Philippi and has him ask it with the title already in his mouth, *the Son of Adam*. What Luke gives next is Peter's answer, *The Messiah (Christ) of Elohim (God)* (Luke 9:20), and nothing is said of a rock or keys.
cards.member_phrase: he asked his disciples, saying, Whom do men say that I the Son of Adam am?
cards.member_sentence: Matthew sets the question at Caesarea Philippi and has Yahusha (Jesus) name himself in it as the Son of Adam.

cards.prose: Luke gives no gap. The order to *tell no man that thing* is followed at once by what the Son of Adam must go through, *and be slain, and be raised the third day* (Luke 9:22), where Matthew marks the turn with *From that time forth* and names Jerusalem as the place. The one just named Messiah (Christ) is told in the same hour what he must suffer.
cards.member_phrase: how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes
cards.member_sentence: Matthew marks the turn at that time and says he must go to Jerusalem and suffer many things from the elders, chief priests and scribes.

cards.prose: Luke has him say it *to them all*, where Matthew has him speak *unto his disciples*, so the saying is open to the whole company that was listening. And Luke alone adds *daily*. The cross is taken up for the length of the walk, not once.
cards.member_sentence: Matthew gives the saying to his disciples without the word daily: deny himself, take up his cross, and follow.

cards.prose: Luke counts *about an eight days* after the sayings where Matthew says *after six days*, and Luke says why he went up: *to pray*. In Luke the glory comes as he prays, and then the Father's voice speaks over him, *This is my beloved Son: hear him* (Luke 9:35), the voice of the unseen Father over the Son the three men can see.
cards.member_sentence: Matthew counts six days and takes Peter, James and John his brother up an high mountain apart, without saying they went to pray.

cards.prose: Matthew tells what the glory looked like, that *his face did shine as the sun* and his clothes were white as the light. Luke tells who saw it and in what state: Peter and the two with him were *heavy with sleep*, and *when they were awake, they saw his glory*, and the two men standing with him. They were not dreaming it; they woke into it.
cards.member_sentence: Matthew says what the transfiguration looked like: his face shining as the sun and his clothing white as the light.

cards.prose: A village will not take him in, and James and John ask for fire *as Elijah did*. Matthew has already said what a refused house is owed, to shake off the dust and go. Luke has him turn and rebuke them, saying *the Son of Adam is not come to destroy men’s lives, but to save them* (Luke 9:56), and they go to another village.
cards.member_sentence: Matthew gives the answer to a place that will not receive the twelve: they shake off the dust of their feet and leave.
